chunks: What the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me of, from Abū al-Ḥasan Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Dāwūd, from his father, from Abū al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn and Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Do not perform salat (prayer) in a house in which there is khamr or an intoxicant, because the angels do not enter it; and do not perform salat (prayer) in a garment that khamr or an intoxicant has touched until you wash it.

key_terms.الْمَلَائِكَةَ: the angels, whose non-entry is mentioned as the reason
key_terms.بَيْتٍ: a house or dwelling in which the prayer is performed
key_terms.تَغْسِلَهُ: wash it to remove the impurity before salat (prayer)
key_terms.خَمْرٌ: wine or intoxicating liquor treated here as a contaminating substance

ai.seo_question: Can one perform salat (prayer) in a house or garment affected by khamr or other intoxicants?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning salat (prayer) in relation to khamr and intoxicants. It forbids praying in a place containing them and forbids praying in a garment contaminated by them until it is washed, linking the ruling of place and clothing with ritual purity and the presence of angels.
